object_description: half-buried terraced volumes set within a system of retaining walls
geometry_property: fifth facade integrated into the site
design_condition: the volumes exploit the sloping topography as an interplay of terraces held by retaining walls that structure the whole site, with three north-south passages defining four public sectors

positive: The scheme takes advantage of the sloping topography with an interplay of terraces
The retaining wall system structures the entire site and defines four distinct public sectors
The siting of the future school at the top of the block is in line with the station building
The hypogean integration of the volumes returns the architecture to the landscape
It leaves the perspective free from the station to the church
The entrance opens onto an esplanade suggesting an interesting expansion of public space
The crèche can take advantage of the roof terrace to extend its activities outside
The typology provides a fifth facade integrated into the site
The jury appreciates the coherent development of the project
negative: The proposed siting does not resolve the easement to the east
The east-west direction is not accompanied by pedestrian paths
South-facing facades read as retaining walls and offer insufficient opening area for proper lighting
The western openings must light spaces more than ten metres deep
The staircase linking the two levels lacks generosity and is insufficiently developed
The organisation of the nursery spaces in a row is unconvincing
The static system is approximate, with problems of load transfer and excessive spans
The typology involves a relatively large amount of floor space
Visualisations ignore the need for protective barriers
High construction costs are inherent in the chosen design
Environmental issues are poorly assessed, mainly due to a penalising form factor
Fire protection compliance poses various distribution problems
Not asserting the volumetry is questionable here; a plinth would have been more appropriate and closer to the historic buildings
Developing the future school in continuity with this concept will be difficult
